title: Inputs and outputs
text: Inputs: ownship and intruder position/velocity (so, vo, si, vi) as 3-vectors in a local Euclidean frame (m, m/s); lookahead bounds B, T (s); thresholds DTHR, ZTHR (m), TTHR, TCOA (s). Outputs: detection interval [t_in, t_out] within [B, T], or the empty encoding (+inf, -inf); a conflict flag; a violation flag.

title: Threshold domain
text: DTHR, ZTHR > 0 and TTHR, TCOA >= 0. The code does not reject other values: every setter and the 4-argument constructor silently replace a threshold by its absolute value, and zero is accepted.

title: Lookahead domain
text: Interval detection assumes 0 <= B < T. B almost equal to T is an instantaneous check evaluated on [B, B+1]; B > T returns no conflict.

title: Operating ranges and threshold tables
text: Horizontal speed 10-700 kt, vertical speed +/-6000 fpm, altitude 100-50,000 ft, lookahead 180 s. Threshold tables in use: DO-365 DWC Phase I (0.66 nmi / 450 ft / 35 s / 0 s), Phase I preventive (700 ft), Phase II (1500 ft / 450 ft / 0 s), non-cooperative (2200 ft / 450 ft / 0 s), buffered DWC and preventive (1.0 nmi / 450 or 750 ft / 35 s / TCOA 20 s).

title: Finite inputs
text: Positions, velocities, thresholds and lookahead are assumed finite. Nothing in the component checks this; behavior on NaN or infinity is unspecified and is measured by the fuzz check.

title: Only relative state matters
text: All outputs depend only on s = so - si and v = vo - vi (translating both aircraft, or adding the same velocity to both, changes nothing).
pvs: WCV(s, v) is stated on relative vectors

title: Horizontal well-clear violation (modified tau)
text: |s_h|^2 <= D^2, or (HMD^2 <= D^2 and 0 <= taumod <= TTHR), where HMD^2 = |s_h + tcpa*v_h|^2, tcpa = -(s_h.v_h)/|v_h|^2 (0 if v_h = 0), and taumod = (D^2 - |s_h|^2)/(s_h.v_h) if s_h.v_h < 0, else -1.

title: Vertical well-clear violation
text: |sz| <= ZTHR, or 0 <= tcoa <= TCOA where tcoa = -sz/vz if sz*vz < 0, else -1.

title: Well-clear violation is horizontal and vertical violation
text: WCV(s, v) holds if and only if the horizontal (SEM-2) and vertical (SEM-3) conditions both hold.

title: Detection interval is exact
text: For 0 <= B < T and every t in [B, T]: WCV(s + t*v, v) holds if and only if t_in <= t <= t_out. The endpoints are themselves violation times (closed interval).
pvs: WCV_taumod.WCV_taumod_interval_correct (proved in PVS for real arithmetic)

title: Symmetry
text: Exchanging ownship and intruder does not change any output.
code: (consequence of SEM-2/3: both are invariant under (s, v) -> (-s, -v))

title: Conflict flag suppresses near-instantaneous loss
text: conflict <=> t_in < t_out and t_in, t_out are not almost-equal (within 16348 ULPs, or both within 1e-13 of zero). The PVS detection function reports a conflict even when the violation set is a single instant; the code deliberately does not.
pvs: differs from WCV.WCV_detection at single-instant contacts

title: Violation flag is derived from detection on [0, 1]
text: violation <=> detection on [0, 1] reports a conflict whose t_in is almost 0. Consequence: a state that touches the well-clear boundary only at t = 0 (for example exactly at DTHR and moving away) is not a violation, although WCV(s, v) holds at that instant.
pvs: differs from WCV(s, v) on the boundary set

title: Level-flight snap
text: A relative vertical speed with |vz| < 1e-13 m/s is treated as exactly zero.

title: Stationary-geometry snap
text: If |v_h|^2 < 1e-13 m^2/s^2 and |s_h| <= DTHR at the start of the vertical window, relative horizontal motion is treated as zero and the horizontal condition holds for the whole window. Consequence: when |s_h| is within about sqrt(1e-13)*T (6e-5 m for T = 180 s) of DTHR and the aircraft drift apart, the reported exit time can be later than the exact one by up to the whole lookahead. Preserved as a convention for drop-in equivalence.
history: Refined after oracle run 1: the first version stated the snap but not its consequence; the exact oracle found 2 of 600 near-stationary vectors where DAIDALUS reported 180 s of violation against an exact exit at 6.9 s and 175 s.

title: Closed boundaries
text: Every threshold comparison is <=, so boundary points are inside the well-clear violation volume.

title: Tangency tolerance in the circle-exit root
text: When the circle-exit discriminant is within 16348 ULPs of zero it is treated as zero (tangent) instead of producing NaN.

title: Semantic cliffs are a declared boundary band
text: The conflict decision is discontinuous at HMD = DTHR (the horizontal interval jumps from length TTHR to empty), at |s_h| = DTHR with zero relative horizontal velocity, and at |sz| = ZTHR in level flight. Inputs within relative margin 1e-9 of a cliff, or whose exact violation set is shorter than 1e-6 s (or misses by less than 1e-6 s), or that sit on a 1e-13 snap threshold (NUM-1/NUM-2), are boundary-band: any answer is accepted but recorded. Outside the band, answers are graded against the exact semantics with the NUM-1/NUM-2 conventions applied.
code: (derived by analysis of SEM-2/3; not stated in code or PVS)
history: Refined after oracle run 1: grading now applies the NUM-1/NUM-2 conventions, and the pure exact semantics is kept alongside so the convention gap is reported rather than hidden.

title: Accuracy outside the band
text: Outside the boundary band, conflict and violation decisions equal the exact semantics (SEM-2..8) and interval endpoints are within 1e-6 s of the exact endpoints.

title: Constant time
text: Closed-form evaluation: no loops or iteration; cost per call is independent of the inputs.

title: Throughput no worse than the original
text: Single-thread calls per second on the same vectors must be at least the original's.

title: Explicit errors instead of silent answers
text: Reject non-finite inputs, out-of-domain thresholds and malformed lookahead with an explicit error (the original sanitizes or silently computes; see ENV-1, ENV-4).

title: Memory-safe, panic-free
text: No unsafe code; no panic for any input bit pattern.

title: No heap allocation per call
text: The hot path allocates nothing (the original allocates vector and interval objects on every call).
